60	// newConnectivityTestForm creates a ConnectivityTestForm pre-filled with the source container.
61	func newConnectivityTestForm(sourceContainer, networkID, diagnosticImage string, containers []docker.NetworkContainer, width, height int) *ConnectivityTestForm {
62		targetInput := textinput.New()
63		targetInput.Placeholder = "IP or container name  (↑↓ to browse)"
64		targetInput.CharLimit = 100
65		theme.StyleTextInput(&targetInput)
66		targetInput.Focus()
67	
68		portInput := textinput.New()
69		portInput.Placeholder = "80"
70		portInput.CharLimit = 6
71		theme.StyleTextInput(&portInput)
72	
73		return &ConnectivityTestForm{
74			sourceContainer:  sourceContainer,
75			networkID:        networkID,
76			diagnosticImage:  diagnosticImage,
77			containers:       containers,
78			containerListIdx: -1,
79			targetInput:      targetInput,
80			portInput:        portInput,
81			testType:         testPing,
82			focusedField:     cFieldTarget,
83			state:            connectivityStateInput,
84			width:            width,
85			height:           height,
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// isPortActive reports whether the port field should be shown (curl or netcat mode).
90	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) isPortActive() bool {
91		return f.testType == testCurl || f.testType == testNetcat
92	}
93	
94	// numFields returns the total number of navigable fields based on the current test type.
95	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) numFields() int {
96		if f.isPortActive() {
97			return 4 // target, type, port, submit
98		}
99		return 3 // target, type, submit
100	}
101	
102	// submitIdx returns the field index of the submit button.
103	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) submitIdx() int {
104		if f.isPortActive() {
105			return cFieldSubmit
106		}
107		return cFieldPort // submit is at index 2 when port is hidden
108	}
109	
110	// updateFocus applies focus/blur to text inputs based on focusedField.
111	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) updateFocus() {
112		f.targetInput.Blur()
113		f.portInput.Blur()
114		switch f.focusedField {
115		case cFieldTarget:
116			f.targetInput.Focus()
117		case cFieldPort:
118			if f.isPortActive() {
119				f.portInput.Focus()
120			}
121		}
122	}
123	
124	// applyContainerSelection fills the target input with the highlighted container's IPv4.
125	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) applyContainerSelection() {
126		if f.containerListIdx >= 0 && f.containerListIdx < len(f.containers) {
127			f.targetInput.SetValue(f.containers[f.containerListIdx].IPv4)
128		}
129	}
130	
131	// buildCommand returns the CLI arguments for the selected test type and inputs.
132	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) buildCommand() []string {
133		target := strings.TrimSpace(f.targetInput.Value())
134		port := strings.TrimSpace(f.portInput.Value())
135		if port == "" {
136			port = "80"
137		}
138		switch f.testType {
139		case testCurl:
140			return []string{"curl", "-v", "-s", "-m", "5", "http://" + target + ":" + port}
141		case testNetcat:
142			return []string{"nc", "-zv", "-w", "5", target, port}
143		default: // testPing
144			return []string{"ping", "-c", "3", target}
145		}
146	}
147	
148	// SetResult updates the form with the diagnostic test result (called from parent Update).
149	// If both output and an error are present, the test ran but exited with a non-zero code
150	// (e.g. curl exit 52 = empty reply). We treat this as a warning rather than a hard failure.
151	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) SetResult(output string, err error) {
152		f.state = connectivityStateResults
153		f.result = output
154		f.resultScroll = 0
155		if err != nil {
156			// Strip the "diagnostic command failed: " wrapper added by RunDiagnosticContainer
157			errMsg := strings.TrimPrefix(err.Error(), "diagnostic command failed: ")
158			f.resultErr = errMsg
159			// If there is output, the container ran but exited non-zero (e.g. curl/nc exit codes)
160			f.resultExitCode = output != ""
161		} else {
162			f.resultErr = ""
163			f.resultExitCode = false
164		}
165	}
166	
167	// Update handles input events for the connectivity form.
168	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*ConnectivityTestForm, tea.Cmd) {
169		// Block input while running
170		if f.state == connectivityStateRunning {
171			return f, nil
172		}
173	
174		// Results state: scroll with ↑/↓, enter resets to input
175		if f.state == connectivityStateResults {
176			if key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
177				resultLines := strings.Split(f.result, "\n")
178				visibleLines := f.resultVisibleLines()
179				switch key.String() {
180				case "enter":
181					f.state = connectivityStateInput
182					f.result = ""
183					f.resultErr = ""
184					f.resultExitCode = false
185					f.resultScroll = 0
186				case "up", "k":
187					if f.resultScroll > 0 {
188						f.resultScroll--
189					}
190				case "down", "j":
191					maxScroll := max(len(resultLines)-visibleLines, 0)
192					if f.resultScroll < maxScroll {
193						f.resultScroll++
194					}
195				case "g", "home":
196					f.resultScroll = 0
197				case "G", "end":
198					f.resultScroll = max(len(resultLines)-visibleLines, 0)
199				}
200			}
201			return f, nil
202		}
203	
204		switch msg := msg.(type) {
205		case tea.KeyMsg:
206			switch msg.String() {
207			case "up":
208				// On target field with containers: scroll suggestion list up
209				if f.focusedField == cFieldTarget && len(f.containers) > 0 && f.containerListIdx >= 0 {
210					if f.containerListIdx > 0 {
211						f.containerListIdx--
212					} else {
213						f.containerListIdx = -1
214					}
215					f.applyContainerSelection()
216					return f, nil
217				}
218				// Otherwise: navigate to previous field (Rule 135)
219				f.containerListIdx = -1
220				n := f.numFields()
221				f.focusedField = (f.focusedField - 1 + n) % n
222				f.updateFocus()
223				return f, nil
224	
225			case "down":
226				// On target field with containers: scroll suggestion list down
227				if f.focusedField == cFieldTarget && len(f.containers) > 0 && f.containerListIdx < len(f.containers)-1 {
228					f.containerListIdx++
229					f.applyContainerSelection()
230					return f, nil
231				}
232				// Otherwise: navigate to next field (Rule 135)
233				f.containerListIdx = -1
234				f.focusedField = (f.focusedField + 1) % f.numFields()
235				f.updateFocus()
236				return f, nil
237	
238			case "left":
239				if f.focusedField == cFieldType {
240					n := len(testTypeLabels)
241					f.testType = connectivityTestType((int(f.testType) - 1 + n) % n)
242					if !f.isPortActive() && f.focusedField >= f.numFields() {
243						f.focusedField = f.numFields() - 1
244					}
245					f.updateFocus()
246				}
247				return f, nil
248	
249			case "right":
250				if f.focusedField == cFieldType {
251					n := len(testTypeLabels)
252					f.testType = connectivityTestType((int(f.testType) + 1) % n)
253					if !f.isPortActive() && f.focusedField >= f.numFields() {
254						f.focusedField = f.numFields() - 1
255					}
256					f.updateFocus()
257				}
258				return f, nil
259	
260			case "enter":
261				if f.focusedField == f.submitIdx() {
262					target := strings.TrimSpace(f.targetInput.Value())
263					if target == "" {
264						return f, nil
265					}
266					f.state = connectivityStateRunning
267					networkID := f.networkID
268					command := f.buildCommand()
269					return f, runDiagnosticContainerCmd(networkID, f.diagnosticImage, command)
270				}
271			}
272		}
273	
274		// Forward unhandled keys to the focused text input
275		// Any key reaching this point resets the container suggestion selection
276		var cmd tea.Cmd
277		switch f.focusedField {
278		case cFieldTarget:
279			if _, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg); ok {
280				f.containerListIdx = -1
281			}
282			f.targetInput, cmd = f.targetInput.Update(msg)
283		case cFieldPort:
284			if f.isPortActive() {
285				f.portInput, cmd = f.portInput.Update(msg)
286			}
287		}
288		return f, cmd
289	}

291	// View renders the connectivity test form (full viewport, Rule 112).

349			var portLine string

351				portLine = theme.PadWithBg(theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+portLabel)+f.portInput.View(), w)
352			} else {
353				portLine = theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  "+portLabel)+f.portInput.View(), w)
354			}
355			lines = append(lines, portLine, theme.EmptyLineBg(w))
356		}
357	
358		// Submit button
359		submitFocused := f.focusedField == f.submitIdx()
360		lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  ")+theme.RenderButton("Run Test", submitFocused, "primary"), w))
361		return lines
362	}
363	
364	// renderSuggestions renders the navigable container list below the target input.
365	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) renderSuggestions(w int) []string {
366		lines := make([]string, 0, len(f.containers)+1)
367		// Section header
368		lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("    Containers on this network:"), w))
369		for i, c := range f.containers {
370			name := c.Name
371			ip := c.IPv4
372			if ip == "" {
373				ip = "—"
374			}
375			selected := i == f.containerListIdx
376			// Name padded to align IP column
377			namePadded := name
378			if len(namePadded) < 24 {
379				namePadded += strings.Repeat(" ", 24-len(namePadded))
380			}
381			entry := namePadded + "  " + ip
382			var line string
383			if selected {
384				line = theme.PadWithBg(
385					lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight).Bold(true).Render("    "+theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+entry),
386					w,
387				)
388			} else {
389				line = theme.PadWithBg(theme.DimStyle.Render("      "+entry), w)
390			}
391			lines = append(lines, line)
392		}
393		return lines
394	}
395	
396	// resultVisibleLines returns how many output lines fit in the viewport.
397	// Header (3) + status (1) + empty (1) + empty (1) = 6 fixed lines (no inline help per Rule 134).
398	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) resultVisibleLines() int {
399		return max(f.height-6, 3)
400	}
401	
402	// truncateResultLine truncates a plain-text line to maxRunes visible characters,
403	// appending "…" when truncation occurs. CLI output has no ANSI codes, so rune
404	// counting is sufficient and safe.
405	func truncateResultLine(s string, maxRunes int) string {
406		if maxRunes <= 0 {
407			return ""
408		}
409		runes := []rune(s)
410		if len(runes) <= maxRunes {
411			return s
412		}
413		return string(runes[:maxRunes-1]) + "…"
414	}
415	
416	func (f *ConnectivityTestForm) renderResults(w int) []string {
417		var lines []string
418	
419		// Status header
420		switch {
421		case f.resultErr != "" && !f.resultExitCode:
422			// Hard failure: no output, only error
423			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconError+" "+f.resultErr), w))
424		case f.resultErr != "" && f.resultExitCode:
425			// Non-zero exit but output present (e.g. curl exit 52, nc exit 1)
426			warnStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorWarn)
427			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(warnStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconWarning+" "+f.resultErr), w))
428		default:
429			okStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorOK)
430			lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(okStyle.Render("  "+theme.IconOK+" Test completed"), w))
431		}
432		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(w))
433	
434		// Scrollable output
435		if f.result != "" {
436			allLines := strings.Split(f.result, "\n")
437			visible := f.resultVisibleLines()
438			end := min(f.resultScroll+visible, len(allLines))
439			maxContent := w - 3 // 2 indent + 1 for "…"
440			for _, line := range allLines[f.resultScroll:end] {
441				line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r") // strip Windows-style CR
442				line = truncateResultLine(line, maxContent)
443				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  "+line), w))
444			}
445			// Scroll indicator when content overflows
446			if len(allLines) > visible {
447				indicator := theme.DimStyle.Render(
448					fmt.Sprintf("  [%d–%d / %d lines]", f.resultScroll+1, end, len(allLines)),
449				)
450				lines = append(lines, theme.PadWithBg(indicator, w))
451			}
452		}
453	
454		lines = append(lines, theme.EmptyLineBg(w))
455		return lines
456	}

1	package ociresources
2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
5		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/cache"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
12	)
13	
14	// browserState tracks which screen the browser is on.
15	type browserState int
16	
17	const (
18		browserStateInput     browserState = iota // search form
19		browserStateTags                          // results table
20		browserStateStatus                        // spinner during pull
21		browserStateResolving                     // detecting group members
22	)
23	
24	// browserRegistryEntry is one selectable registry in the browser form.
25	// Group members have ParentAlias set; normal registries have it empty.
26	type browserRegistryEntry struct {
27		URL         string
28		Alias       string
29		ParentAlias string // non-empty = member of a group
30		parentURL   string // URL of the parent RegistryItem (for credential lookup)
31	}
32	
33	const brFieldRepo = 0
34	
35	// brFieldReg returns the form field index for the i-th registry checkbox.
36	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldReg(i int) int { return 1 + i }
37	
38	// brFieldSubmit returns the form field index for the Browse Tags button.
39	func (b *RegistryBrowser) brFieldSubmit() int { return 1 + len(b.entries) }
40	
41	// RegistryBrowserCloseMsg is sent when the user presses ESC on the browser input screen.
42	type RegistryBrowserCloseMsg struct{}
43	
44	// tagSortField selects which column to sort the tag list by.
45	type tagSortField int
46	
47	const (
48		tagSortByName    tagSortField = iota
49		tagSortByUpdated              // newest first
50	)
51	
52	// RegistryBrowser searches image tags across multiple configured registries.
53	type RegistryBrowser struct {
54		registries    []config.RegistryItem
55		width, height int
56	
57		// Group detection state
58		entryGroups       [][]browserRegistryEntry // one slot per registry, filled as detections complete
59		entries           []browserRegistryEntry   // flattened from entryGroups after all detections
60		pendingDetections int
61	
62		// Form state
63		repoInput    textinput.Model
64		selectedRegs map[string]bool // entry URL → checked
65		focusedField int
66	
67		// Results state
68		tags              []MultiRegistryTag
69		pendingSearches   int
70		registryFilter    string // "" = all, otherwise filter by RegistryURL
71		tagTable          table.Model
72		scanCache         map[string]cache.ImageScanEntry
73		scanningTags      map[string]bool
74		tagScanSpinnerIdx int
75	
76		// Tag filter/sort in results view
77		filterInput  textinput.Model
78		filterActive bool
79		tagSortCol   tagSortField
80		tagSortDesc  bool
81	
82		// Status screen (pull operation)
83		spinner   spinner.Model
84		operation string
85		imageName string
86	
87		state browserState
88	}
89	
90	// newRegistryBrowser creates a RegistryBrowser and fires group-detection commands for all
91	// configured registries. The browser starts in browserStateResolving until all detections
92	// complete; it then transitions to browserStateInput with the resolved entry list.
93	func newRegistryBrowser(registries []config.RegistryItem, width, height int) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
94		repoInput := textinput.New()
95		repoInput.Placeholder = "nginx  (or library/nginx)"
96		repoInput.CharLimit = 256

167	// HandleGroupDetected incorporates one detection result into the ordered entry list.
168	// When all detections have completed it finalizes entries and switches to input state.
169	func (b *RegistryBrowser) HandleGroupDetected(msg RegistryGroupDetectedMsg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
170		for i, reg := range b.registries {
171			if reg.URL != msg.RegistryURL {
172				continue
173			}
174			alias := reg.Alias
175			if alias == "" {
176				alias = reg.URL
177			}
178			if len(msg.Members) > 0 {
179				group := make([]browserRegistryEntry, len(msg.Members))
180				for j, m := range msg.Members {
181					group[j] = browserRegistryEntry{
182						URL:         m.URL,
183						Alias:       m.Alias,
184						ParentAlias: alias,
185						parentURL:   reg.URL,
186					}
187				}
188				b.entryGroups[i] = group
189			} else {
190				b.entryGroups[i] = []browserRegistryEntry{{URL: reg.URL, Alias: alias}}
191			}
192			break
193		}
194		b.pendingDetections--
195		if b.pendingDetections <= 0 {
196			b.finalizeEntries()
197		}
198		return b, nil
199	}
200	
201	// finalizeEntries flattens entryGroups into entries, initialises selectedRegs (all checked),
202	// and transitions the browser to the input form state.
203	func (b *RegistryBrowser) finalizeEntries() {
204		b.entries = nil
205		for _, group := range b.entryGroups {
206			b.entries = append(b.entries, group...)
207		}
208		b.selectedRegs = make(map[string]bool, len(b.entries))
209		for _, e := range b.entries {
210			b.selectedRegs[e.URL] = true
211		}
212		b.state = browserStateInput
213		b.updateFocus()
214	}

216	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeInputs() {
217		w := max(b.width-22, 20)
218		b.repoInput.Width = w
219		b.filterInput.Width = max(b.width-6, 10)
220	}
221	
222	func (b *RegistryBrowser) resizeTagTable() {
223		b.tagTable.SetHeight(max(b.height, 1))
224	
225		// b.width is already the viewport content width (full width - 2 borders).
226		// Subtract only the cell padding (numCols × 2) so column widths sum exactly to `available`.
227		const numCols = 7
228		available := max(b.width-numCols*2, 10)
229		fixedReg := 20
230		fixedUpdated := 16
231		fixedC, fixedH, fixedM := 4, 4, 4
232		fixedSum := fixedReg + fixedUpdated + fixedC + fixedH + fixedM
233		flexTag := max(available-fixedSum-4, 8) // reserve 4 for last col minimum
234	
235		cols := b.tagTable.Columns()
236		if len(cols) == numCols {
237			cols[0].Width = fixedReg
238			cols[1].Width = flexTag
239			cols[2].Width = fixedUpdated
240			cols[3].Width = fixedC
241			cols[4].Width = fixedH
242			cols[5].Width = fixedM
243			// Last column absorbs leftover so sum(col_widths) == available exactly.
244			cols[6].Width = available - fixedReg - flexTag - fixedUpdated - fixedC - fixedH - fixedM
245			b.tagTable.SetColumns(cols)
246		}
247	
248		// Force the Selected row style to span the viewport content width so the selected
249		// background extends to the right border, even when row content visually differs
250		// from the calculated width (e.g. Nerd Font icon width discrepancies). See workspaces fix.
251		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
252		styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(b.width)
253		b.tagTable.SetStyles(styles)
254	}

12	// InEditMode returns true when a text input is active (blocks command mode).
13	func (b *RegistryBrowser) InEditMode() bool {
14		if b.state == browserStateResolving {
15			return false

23	// IsSearching returns true while registry tag queries are still in flight.
24	func (b *RegistryBrowser) IsSearching() bool {
25		return b.pendingSearches > 0
26	}

28	// Update handles all messages for the browser.
29	func (b *RegistryBrowser) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
30		switch msg := msg.(type) {
31		case tea.KeyMsg:
32			return b.handleKeyMsg(msg)
33		case spinner.TickMsg:
34			if b.state == browserStateStatus || b.state == browserStateResolving || len(b.scanningTags) > 0 || b.pendingSearches > 0 {
35				var cmd tea.Cmd
36				b.spinner, cmd = b.spinner.Update(msg)
37				if b.state == browserStateTags && len(b.scanningTags) > 0 {
38					b.tagScanSpinnerIdx++
39					b.rebuildTagTable()
40				}
41				return b, cmd
42			}
43			return b, nil
44		}
45		return b.delegateUpdate(msg)
46	}
47	
48	func (b *RegistryBrowser) delegateUpdate(msg tea.Msg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
49		if b.state == browserStateInput && b.focusedField == brFieldRepo {
50			var cmd tea.Cmd
51			b.repoInput, cmd = b.repoInput.Update(msg)
52			return b, cmd
53		}
54		if b.state == browserStateTags {
55			if b.filterActive {
56				var cmd tea.Cmd
57				b.filterInput, cmd = b.filterInput.Update(msg)
58				b.rebuildTagTable()
59				return b, cmd
60			}
61			var cmd tea.Cmd
62			b.tagTable, cmd = b.tagTable.Update(msg)
63			return b, cmd
64		}
65		return b, nil
66	}
67	
68	func (b *RegistryBrowser) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
69		switch b.state {
70		case browserStateResolving:
71			return b, nil
72		case browserStateInput:
73			return b.handleInputKeyMsg(msg)
74		case browserStateTags:
75			return b.handleTagsKeyMsg(msg)
76		case browserStateStatus:
77			return b, nil
78		}
79		return b, nil
80	}
81	
82	func (b *RegistryBrowser) handleInputKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
83		switch msg.String() {
84		case "esc":
85			return b, func() tea.Msg { return RegistryBrowserCloseMsg{} }
86		case "down":
87			b.focusedField = min(b.focusedField+1, b.brFieldSubmit())
88			b.updateFocus()
89			return b, nil
90		case "up":
91			b.focusedField = max(b.focusedField-1, brFieldRepo)
92			b.updateFocus()
93			return b, nil
94		case " ":
95			if b.focusedField >= 1 && b.focusedField <= len(b.entries) {
96				url := b.entries[b.focusedField-1].URL
97				b.selectedRegs[url] = !b.selectedRegs[url]
98				return b, nil
99			}
100		case "enter":
101			if b.focusedField == brFieldRepo || b.focusedField == b.brFieldSubmit() {
102				return b.submitSearch()
103			}
104			b.focusedField = min(b.focusedField+1, b.brFieldSubmit())
105			b.updateFocus()
106			return b, nil
107		}
108		return b.delegateUpdate(msg)
109	}
110	
111	func (b *RegistryBrowser) submitSearch() (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
112		repo := strings.TrimSpace(b.repoInput.Value())
113		if repo == "" {
114			return b, nil
115		}
116	
117		b.tags = nil
118		b.registryFilter = ""
119		b.pendingSearches = 0
120		b.filterInput.SetValue("")
121		b.filterActive = false
122		b.tagSortCol = tagSortByName
123		b.tagSortDesc = false
124	
125		var cmds []tea.Cmd
126		for _, entry := range b.entries {
127			if !b.selectedRegs[entry.URL] {
128				continue
129			}
130			// Credentials come from the parent registry (or the entry itself for normal registries).
131			credURL := entry.URL
132			if entry.parentURL != "" {
133				credURL = entry.parentURL
134			}
135			var username string
136			for _, reg := range b.registries {
137				if reg.URL == credURL {
138					username = reg.Username
139					break
140				}
141			}
142			storedUser, storedPass, _ := docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)
143			if username == "" {
144				username = storedUser
145			}
146			alias := entry.Alias
147			if entry.ParentAlias != "" {
148				alias = entry.ParentAlias + "/" + entry.Alias
149			}
150			normalizedRepo := normalizeRepoForRegistry(entry.URL, repo)
151			apiURL := registryAPIURL(entry.URL)
152			b.pendingSearches++
153			cmds = append(cmds, searchRegistryTagsCmd(entry.URL, alias, apiURL, normalizedRepo, username, storedPass))
154		}
155	
156		if len(cmds) == 0 {
157			return b, nil
158		}
159	
160		b.state = browserStateTags
161		b.tagTable.Focus()
162		b.rebuildTagTable()
163		cmds = append(cmds, b.spinner.Tick)
164		return b, tea.Batch(cmds...)
165	}
166	
167	func (b *RegistryBrowser) handleTagsKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (*RegistryBrowser, tea.Cmd) {
168		if b.filterActive {
169			switch msg.String() {
170			case "esc", "enter":
171				b.filterActive = false
172				b.filterInput.Blur()
173				b.rebuildTagTable()
174				b.resizeTagTable()
175				return b, nil
176			}
177			return b.delegateUpdate(msg)
178		}
179	
180		switch msg.String() {
181		case "esc":
182			b.state = browserStateInput
183			b.tagTable.Blur()
184			b.updateFocus()
185			return b, nil
186		case "/":
187			b.filterActive = true
188			b.filterInput.Focus()
189			b.resizeTagTable()
190			return b, nil
191		case ".":
192			b.cycleSortTags()
193			return b, nil
194		case "r":
195			b.cycleRegistryFilter()
196			return b, nil
197		case "up", "k":
198			b.tagTable.MoveUp(1)
199			return b, nil
200		case "down", "j":
201			b.tagTable.MoveDown(1)
202			return b, nil
203		case "g", "home":
204			b.tagTable.GotoTop()
205			return b, nil
206		case "G", "end":
207			b.tagTable.GotoBottom()
208			return b, nil
209		case "enter":
210			return b.openTagScanDetails()
211		case "p":
212			return b.pullSelectedTag()
213		case "ctrl+s":
214			return b.requestDirectScan()
215		}
216		return b, nil
217	}

**D14 — the registry filter shows a raw URL for group members.**
`registryFilterLabel()` (`browser_tags.go:63`) resolves the active filter by
searching `b.registries`, which holds only the configured top-level entries.
Discovered members are not in that list, so filtering to one falls through to
returning `b.registryFilter` — the full synthesised URL — where every other row
in the same view shows a short alias. The fix follows from §3.8 rather than
preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
gains a group level at the same time.

Pinned inverted by `TestAGroupMembersFilterLabelIsStillARawURL`, which asserts
the raw URL today and asserts the configured registry's alias alongside it as
the contrast.

**D20 — an image scanned with no scanner installed is reported as clean.** Found
by the phase 6 pass, and the most serious of the three defects it turned up: a
security feature that says an image is fine when nothing looked at it.

`Scanner.Scan` skips a stage whose tool is unavailable rather than failing it
(`scanner.go:303`, `if s.options.EnableVuln && s.deps.TrivyAvailable`), so with
no trivy the result carries **no errors and no findings**. `scanOneImageCmd`
reports a failure only when there are errors *and* no findings
(`commands.go:111`), so the image comes back with zero counts, those counts are
written to the scan cache with a fresh timestamp, and Rule 126 keeps them until
an explicit rescan. Enter then opens an empty report.

Nothing upstream catches it: **`internal/ui/oci_resources` performs no
dependency check at all**, unlike the security view, which gates its scan on
`canStart := m.deps.TrivyAvailable || m.deps.GitleaksAvailable`
(`security/view.go:147`). Every entry point is affected — `ctrl+s`, `A`,
`ctrl+a` and the delegated `LaunchBatchScanMsg` all reach the same
`batchScanCmd`.

Two candidate fixes, and the choice is what makes this worth recording rather
than fixing on the spot:

- **In `internal/scan`** — report "no scanner available" when every enabled
  stage was skipped for want of a tool. It fixes every caller at once and is
  where the knowledge lives, but it changes shared semantics; the security view
  guards upstream, so it would not regress there.
- **In the view** — resolve dependencies as the security view does and refuse
  the scan with a footer message (Rule 128). Narrower, and it tells the user
  *before* they wait rather than after.

The second is the better user-facing answer and the first is the better
guarantee; doing both is defensible.

Pinned inverted by `TestAScanWithNoScannerInstalledIsWronglyReportedAsClean`,
which asserts the empty counts *and* that they reach the disk. That test is what
fails when D20 is fixed.

**D21 — an unreachable focus clamp in `ConnectivityTestForm`.** Dead code, not a
user-visible defect, and the same shape as D5 in `CreationForm`.

The `left` and `right` handlers (`connectivity_form.go:242`, `:253`) clamp the
focus after cycling the test type, guarding against the field count shrinking
from four to three when the port field disappears. It cannot fire: both branches
are inside `if f.focusedField == cFieldType`, so `focusedField` is 1, and
`numFields()` is never below 3.

Fix it the way D5 was: delete both clamps and record why they cannot fire, so
they are not reintroduced defensively. The invariant they were guarding is
already pinned by `TestCyclingTheTypeNeverStrandsTheFocus`, which passes before
and after.

input.new_string:
### Test coverage

**80.7 % overall — the agreed 80 % target is met.**

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `internal/ui/testutil` Bubble Tea harness | **done** (100 %) |
| 1 | Leaf components and pure helpers | **done** except the `ui/theme` complement (~55 stmts) |
| 2 | Mid-size view state machines (`status`, `containers`, `dashboard`, `gitlab/auth`) | **done** |
| 3 | Large views (`workspaces`, `explorer`, `security`, `netdiag`) | **done** |
| 4 | `ui/oci_resources` | **done** — 43.4 %, the rest deferred to phase 6 |
| 5 | Router and I/O seams (`app`, `scan`, `docker`) | **done** — `app` 90.5 %, `scan` 99.2 %, `docker` 65.4 % |
| 6 | Remainder to reach 80 % | **done** — 73.8 % → 80.7 % |

**Phase 5 was complete when phase 6 began.** The three packages needed three
different seams: `app` needed only a constructor that does not read the
terminal, `docker` needed `dockerRunner`, and `scan` needed `commandRunner` plus
pure argument builders. None of them needed a mocking library.

**Phase 6 was one package.** `internal/ui/oci_resources` held 1 509 of the
2 900 uncovered statements in the project, so it was the only one that had to
move: 43.4 % → **73.0 %**, which carried the total from 73.8 % to 80.7 % on its
own. It was left at 43.4 % in phase 4 on the grounds that the rest "wants the
seam phase 5 builds"; that turned out to be half right. What `commands.go`
needed was not the `dockerRunner` seam — which is unexported and therefore
unreachable from this package — but the *other* technique phase 5 produced.

**A fake tool on PATH reaches further than a seam does.** `internal/scan`
installed copies of the test binary as `trivy` and `docker` to steer detection;
the same trick covers `commands.go` end to end, including the error handling in
`internal/docker` underneath it, with no export added anywhere. One extension
was needed: a single fake answers many different commands here — `docker image
ls` and `docker network inspect` reach the same file — so the reply is selected
by **the longest matching invocation prefix** (`faketool_test.go`) rather than
being fixed for the process. A second env var makes each fake append its
invocation to a file, which is what lets a test assert *what docker was asked*;
that is how the "untagged images are scanned by ID, cached by name" rule is
pinned.

The registry half needed no seam at all: every entry point takes the base URL as
an argument, so `httptest` covers the tag search, the bearer-token exchange and
Nexus group detection. `fetchDockerHubTagsMeta` is the one exception — it builds
a `hub.docker.com` URL itself — and swapping `ociHTTPClient` for one whose
transport rewrites the host covers it without changing production code.

`tea.Sequence` had to be taught to `testutil.Msgs`. `tea.Batch` answers with the
exported `tea.BatchMsg`, but the sequence equivalent is unexported, so a
sequenced command reported as one opaque message and the commands inside it
never ran — which is why `scanOneImageCmd` sat at 4.3 % with tests around it.
Its underlying type is `[]tea.Cmd`, so reflection recovers them without
depending on the name (`testutil.sequenced`). That is what made the scan
commands testable, and D20 is what fell out of testing them.

What is deliberately left uncovered in `oci_resources`, at 73.0 %: the
launch-form renderers and the remaining `keys.go` / `view.go` branches. Those
are layout, and pinning them means pinning pixels.

The packages still below target are `internal/registrymgr` (18.5 %),
`internal/oci` (37.3 %), `internal/status` (64.8 %), `internal/docker` (65.4 %)
and `internal/cache` (71.3 %) — 470 uncovered statements between them, none of
which the 80 % figure needs. Two are worth doing on their own merits rather than
for the number: `registrymgr`, because §3.8 step 4 rewrites `CanHandle`, and
`oci`, whose gap is the registry HTTP paths that need a manifest-plus-gzipped-
layer fixture rather than the single-response stubs used so far.

**Five open.** Three are in the registry browser and were found while reviewing

coverage pass. See [§1.3](#13-open). D1–D11 and D15–D19 are fixed; §1.1 records

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not

so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

honoured in exactly three places: the `docker login` fired on form submit, the
`Logged` column, and the URL list `registryLoginStatusCmd` checks. Neither code
path that actually talks to a registry consults it. `submitSearch`

test: reach the 80% coverage target (phase 6, internal/ui/oci_resources)

Overall coverage 73.8% -> 80.7%, which closes phase 6 of the plan in §2 of
docs/backlog.md and unblocks §3.8.

One package had to move. internal/ui/oci_resources held 1509 of the 2900
uncovered statements in the project, so taking it from 43.4% to 73.0% carried
the total past the target on its own.

Phase 4 left it there on the grounds that the rest "wants the seam phase 5
builds". That was half right. What commands.go needed was not the dockerRunner
seam — it is unexported and unreachable from this package — but the other
technique phase 5 produced: a copy of the test binary installed on a PATH of
the test's own making, behaving as the tool. That covers the commands end to
end, including the error handling in internal/docker underneath them, with no
export added anywhere.

Two extensions were needed:

- One fake answers many commands here (`docker image ls` and `docker network
  inspect` reach the same file), so the reply is chosen by the longest matching
  invocation prefix rather than fixed for the process.
- A second variable makes each fake append its invocation to a file, which is
  what lets a test assert what docker was asked. That is how "untagged images
  are scanned by ID but cached by name" is pinned.

The registry half needed no seam: every entry point takes a base URL, so
httptest covers the tag search, the bearer-token exchange and Nexus group
detection. fetchDockerHubTagsMeta builds its own hub.docker.com URL, and
swapping ociHTTPClient for one whose transport rewrites the host covers it
without touching production code.

connectivity_form.go (196 statements, 0%) needed nothing at all — a
self-contained form whose only command it returns and never runs. It was
testable the whole time and had been skipped by association with the files
around it.

testutil.Msgs now flattens tea.Sequence as well as tea.Batch. tea.Batch answers
with the exported tea.BatchMsg but the sequence equivalent is unexported, so a
sequenced command reported as one opaque message and the commands inside it
never ran — which is why scanOneImageCmd sat at 4.3% with tests around it. Its
underlying type is []tea.Cmd, so reflection recovers them without depending on
the name.

Two defects found, recorded rather than fixed, each with its test written
inverted per the pattern in §1.2:

- D20: an image scanned with no scanner installed is reported as clean. Scan()
  skips a stage whose tool is missing rather than failing it, so the result
  carries no errors and no findings, and scanOneImageCmd only reports a failure
  when there are errors AND no findings. Zero counts reach the scan cache with
  a fresh timestamp and Rule 126 keeps them. This view performs no dependency
  check at all, unlike the security view. The most serious of the two: a
  security feature saying an image is fine when nothing looked at it.
- D21: an unreachable focus clamp in ConnectivityTestForm, the same shape as D5.
  The invariant it guards is pinned by a test that passes before and after.

D14's inverted test now exists too, alongside the credential-lookup test §3.8
step 2 will turn around.

go vet, golangci-lint and go test are clean. mise run test-race still needs CI
— no C compiler locally.
EOF

Closes phase 6 of the coverage plan in §2 of `docs/backlog.md`. **73.8 % → 80.7 %**, so the agreed 80 % target is met, and §3.8 is unblocked.

## One package had to move

`internal/ui/oci_resources` held **1 509 of the 2 900** uncovered statements in the project, so taking it from 43.4 % to **73.0 %** carried the total past the target on its own.

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.go` | 6.9 % | 88.0 % |
| `connectivity_form.go` | 0.0 % | ~99 % |
| `browser_tags.go` | 3.2 % | ~97 % |
| `browser_view.go` | 1.0 % | ~99 % |
| `browser_keys.go` | 8.6 % | 78.1 % |
| `launch.go` | 0.0 % | ~96 % |

## How, and where phase 4's reasoning was half wrong

Phase 4 left this package at 43.4 % on the grounds that the rest "wants the seam phase 5 builds". What `commands.go` needed was **not** the `dockerRunner` seam — it is unexported and unreachable from this package — but the *other* technique phase 5 produced: **a copy of the test binary installed on a PATH of the test's own making**, behaving as the tool. That covers the commands end to end, including the error handling in `internal/docker` underneath them, with no export added anywhere.

Two extensions were needed (`faketool_test.go`):

- One fake answers many different commands here — `docker image ls` and `docker network inspect` reach the same file — so the reply is chosen by the **longest matching invocation prefix** rather than fixed for the process.
- A second variable makes each fake **append its invocation to a file**, so a test can assert *what docker was asked*. That is how "untagged images are scanned by ID but cached by name" is pinned.

The registry half needed no seam at all: every entry point takes a base URL, so `httptest` covers the tag search, the bearer-token exchange and Nexus group detection. `fetchDockerHubTagsMeta` builds its own `hub.docker.com` URL, and swapping `ociHTTPClient` for one whose transport rewrites the host covers it without touching production code.

And `connectivity_form.go` (196 statements, 0 %) needed **nothing** — a self-contained form whose only command it returns and never runs. It was testable the whole time and had been skipped by association with the files around it. Judge a file by its own dependencies, not by the package it sits in.

## `testutil.Msgs` now flattens `tea.Sequence`

`tea.Batch` answers with the exported `tea.BatchMsg`, but the sequence equivalent is unexported — so a sequenced command reported as one opaque message and the commands inside it never ran. That is why `scanOneImageCmd` sat at 4.3 % with tests around it. Its underlying type is `[]tea.Cmd`, so reflection recovers them without depending on the name. `testutil` stays at 100 %.

## Two defects found, recorded rather than fixed

Each has its test written **inverted**, per the pattern §1.2 established — asserting today's behaviour and saying so, so the test is what fails when the fix lands.

- **D20 — an image scanned with no scanner installed is reported as clean.** `Scan()` skips a stage whose tool is missing rather than failing it, so the result carries no errors and no findings; `scanOneImageCmd` reports a failure only when there are errors **and** no findings. Zero counts reach the scan cache with a fresh timestamp, and Rule 126 keeps them until an explicit rescan. Nothing upstream catches it: this view performs **no dependency check at all**, unlike the security view (`view.go:147`). The more serious of the two — a security feature saying an image is fine when nothing looked at it. Two candidate fixes are written up in the backlog.
- **D21 — an unreachable focus clamp in `ConnectivityTestForm`**, the same shape as D5 in `CreationForm`. Dead code, not user-visible. The invariant it guards is pinned by a test that passes before and after.

D14's inverted test now exists as well, alongside `TestManagementCredentialsAreLookedUpByHostAlone`, which pins the credential behaviour §3.8 step 2 changes. Turn both around rather than deleting them.

The new tests spawn subprocesses and swap `PATH`/`ociHTTPClient` via `t.Setenv` and `t.Cleanup`, so nothing in the package may run in parallel — the same constraint `internal/credentials` documents for `keyring.MockInit`.

CI is green — including `mise run test-race`, which ran clean (no data race), so the new subprocess-spawning tests are safe under the detector.

## Phase 6 terminée — objectif 80 % atteint

**73.8 % → 80.7 %** au total. PR : https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/26 (CI verte, prête à merger — je ne l'ai pas mergée).

### Un seul package a dû bouger

`internal/ui/oci_resources` portait **1 509 des 2 900** statements non couverts du projet. Le faire passer de 43.4 % à **73.0 %** a suffi à franchir la barre.

| Fichier | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.go` | 6.9 % | 88.0 % |
| `connectivity_form.go` | 0.0 % | ~99 % |
| `browser_tags.go` / `browser_view.go` | 3.2 / 1.0 % | ~97 / ~99 % |
| `browser_keys.go` | 8.6 % | 78.1 % |
| `launch.go` | 0.0 % | ~96 % |

### Le raisonnement de la phase 4 était à moitié faux

Elle avait laissé le package là en disant que le reste « attend le seam de la phase 5 ». Ce dont `commands.go` avait besoin, ce n'était **pas** `dockerRunner` — non exporté, donc inatteignable depuis ce package — mais l'*autre* technique de la phase 5 : une copie du binaire de test installée sur un PATH fabriqué par le test. Ça couvre les commandes de bout en bout, y compris la gestion d'erreur d'`internal/docker` en dessous, sans rien exporter.

Deux extensions : le faux outil répond selon le **préfixe d'invocation le plus long** (un seul fake sert `docker image ls` et `docker network inspect`), et il **journalise ce qu'on lui a demandé** — c'est ce qui permet d'épingler « une image sans tag est scannée par ID mais cachée par nom ».

Et `connectivity_form.go` (196 statements, 0 %) n'avait besoin de **rien** : formulaire autonome, testable depuis toujours, sauté par association avec les fichiers voisins.

`testutil.Msgs` aplatit maintenant `tea.Sequence` en plus de `tea.Batch` (le type de message équivalent n'est pas exporté ; la réflexion le récupère par sa forme `[]tea.Cmd`). C'est ce qui débloquait `scanOneImageCmd`, bloqué à 4.3 % malgré des tests autour.

### Deux défauts trouvés, enregistrés avec test inversé

- **D20 — une image scannée sans scanner installé est rapportée comme saine.** `Scan()` *saute* l'étape dont l'outil manque au lieu de la faire échouer → aucune erreur, aucun finding → `scanOneImageCmd` conclut « propre », écrit des compteurs à zéro dans le cache avec un timestamp frais, et la Rule 126 les y garde. Rien en amont ne rattrape : cette vue **ne vérifie aucune dépendance**, contrairement à la vue security. C'est le plus grave — une fonction de sécurité qui affirme qu'une image est saine alors que rien ne l'a regardée. Deux pistes de correction sont écrites dans le backlog.
- **D21 — un clamp de focus inatteignable** dans `ConnectivityTestForm`, même forme que D5. Code mort, pas visible pour l'utilisateur.

§3.8 est débloqué : le split (phase 4) et la couverture (phase 6) sont faits, et les tests inversés de D14 et du lookup de credentials sont en place pour être retournés quand la feature atterrira.

**Prochaine étape recommandée : D20**, en PR de correction séparée — c'est le seul défaut ouvert qui donne un faux résultat de sécurité. Je merge la #26 d'abord ?

90	// runTrivy executes a built invocation and parses what it wrote to stdout.
91	//
92	// A non-zero exit is not on its own a failure: Trivy exits 1 when it finds
93	// vulnerabilities, and the report on stdout is exactly what the caller asked
94	// for. Only an exit that produced no report is reported as an error.
95	func runTrivy(ctx context.Context, tc toolCmd, progressFn func(string)) ([]Finding, error) {
96		stdout, err := runner.Run(ctx, tc, progressFn)
97		if err != nil {
98			var exit *exitError
99			if !errors.As(err, &exit) || len(stdout) == 0 {
100				return nil, fmt.Errorf("trivy failed: %w", err)
101			}
102		}
103		return parseTrivyOutput(stdout)
104	}

106	// parseTrivyOutput parses Trivy JSON output into findings
107	func parseTrivyOutput(data []byte) ([]Finding, error) {
108		var report TrivyReport
109		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &report); err != nil {
110			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse trivy output: %w", err)
111		}
112	
113		var findings []Finding
114	
115		for _, result := range report.Results {
116			// Process vulnerabilities
117			for _, vuln := range result.Vulnerabilities {
118				// Build references from PrimaryURL and advisory links
119				refs := make([]string, 0, len(vuln.References)+1)
120				if vuln.PrimaryURL != "" {
121					refs = append(refs, vuln.PrimaryURL)
122				}
123				for _, r := range vuln.References {
124					if r != vuln.PrimaryURL {
125						refs = append(refs, r)
126					}
127				}
128	
129				// Build a fix command suggestion when a fixed version is known
130				fixCmd := ""
131				if vuln.FixedVersion != "" {
132					fixCmd = fmt.Sprintf("Update %s to %s", vuln.PkgName, vuln.FixedVersion)
133				}
134	
135				findings = append(findings, Finding{
136					ID:          vuln.VulnerabilityID,
137					Title:       vuln.Title,
138					Description: vuln.Description,
139					Severity:    parseSeverity(vuln.Severity),
140					Source:      "trivy",
141					File:        result.Target,
142					PkgName:     vuln.PkgName,
143					Version:     vuln.InstalledVersion,
144					FixedIn:     vuln.FixedVersion,
145					References:  refs,
146					FixCommand:  fixCmd,
147				})
148			}
149	
150			// Process licenses found by Trivy
151			for _, license := range result.Licenses {
152				findings = append(findings, Finding{
153					ID:          license.Name,
154					Title:       fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", license.PkgName, license.Name),
155					Description: fmt.Sprintf("License category: %s", license.Category),
156					Severity:    parseSeverity(license.Severity),
157					Source:      "trivy-license",
158					File:        license.FilePath,
159					PkgName:     license.PkgName,
160				})
161			}
162	
163			// Process misconfigurations found by Trivy
164			for _, misconf := range result.Misconfigurations {
165				var miscRefs []string
166				if misconf.PrimaryURL != "" {
167					miscRefs = append(miscRefs, misconf.PrimaryURL)
168				}
169				findings = append(findings, Finding{
170					ID:          misconf.AVDID,
171					Title:       misconf.Title,
172					Description: misconf.Desc,
173					Severity:    parseSeverity(misconf.Severity),
174					Source:      "trivy-misconfig",
175					File:        result.Target,
176					Line:        misconf.CauseMetadata.StartLine,
177					Resolution:  misconf.Resolution,
178					References:  miscRefs,
179				})
180			}
181		}
182	
183		return findings, nil
184	}

**D20 — an image scanned with no scanner installed is reported as clean.** Found
by the phase 6 pass, and the most serious of the three defects it turned up: a
security feature that says an image is fine when nothing looked at it.

`Scanner.Scan` skips a stage whose tool is unavailable rather than failing it
(`scanner.go:303`, `if s.options.EnableVuln && s.deps.TrivyAvailable`), so with
no trivy the result carries **no errors and no findings**. `scanOneImageCmd`
reports a failure only when there are errors *and* no findings
(`commands.go:111`), so the image comes back with zero counts, those counts are
written to the scan cache with a fresh timestamp, and Rule 126 keeps them until
an explicit rescan. Enter then opens an empty report.

Nothing upstream catches it: **`internal/ui/oci_resources` performs no
dependency check at all**, unlike the security view, which gates its scan on
`canStart := m.deps.TrivyAvailable || m.deps.GitleaksAvailable`
(`security/view.go:147`). Every entry point is affected — `ctrl+s`, `A`,
`ctrl+a` and the delegated `LaunchBatchScanMsg` all reach the same
`batchScanCmd`.

Two candidate fixes, and the choice is what makes this worth recording rather
than fixing on the spot:

- **In `internal/scan`** — report "no scanner available" when every enabled
  stage was skipped for want of a tool. It fixes every caller at once and is
  where the knowledge lives, but it changes shared semantics; the security view
  guards upstream, so it would not regress there.
- **In the view** — resolve dependencies as the security view does and refuse
  the scan with a footer message (Rule 128). Narrower, and it tells the user
  *before* they wait rather than after.

The second is the better user-facing answer and the first is the better
guarantee; doing both is defensible.

input.old_string: ### 1.2 The five parked defects
input.new_string:
**D20 — an image scanned with no scanner installed was reported as clean.**
Found by the phase 6 coverage pass, and the most serious defect this repository
has recorded: a security feature that says an image is fine when nothing looked
at it.

`Scanner.Scan` **skips** a stage whose tool is unavailable rather than failing
it (`if s.options.EnableVuln && s.deps.TrivyAvailable`), so with no trivy the
result carried **no errors and no findings**. `scanOneImageCmd` reports a
failure only when there are errors *and* no findings, so the image came back
with zero counts, those counts were written to the scan cache with a fresh
timestamp, and Rule 126 kept them until an explicit rescan. Enter then opened an
empty report.

Nothing upstream caught it: `internal/ui/oci_resources` performs no dependency
check at all, unlike the security view, which gates its scan on
`canStart := m.deps.TrivyAvailable || m.deps.GitleaksAvailable`
(`security/view.go:147`). Every entry point was affected — `ctrl+s`, `A`,
`ctrl+a` and the delegated `LaunchBatchScanMsg` all reach the same
`batchScanCmd`.

**Fix:** `Scan` now records a missing tool as an error, in
`missingToolErrors`, before any stage starts. That is one change in the package
where the knowledge lives and it closes the defect for every caller — the OCI
images view needed no change at all, because `scanOneImageCmd`'s existing
"errors and no findings" condition then reports the failure by itself. Adding a
dependency check to the view was considered and dropped: with no scanner the
scan returns instantly, so a pre-flight guard buys nothing a clear error does
not.

The precision that makes it usable is in **what is not reported**. A stage
skipped because it does not apply to the target type is not missing anything —
gitleaks scans a working tree, so a secret scan of an image was never going to
run — and reporting those would train the user to ignore the warnings panel.
Only stages that would otherwise have run are named, and each message says what
to install (`install trivy or pull aquasec/trivy`).

This reversed a decision the tests had recorded.
`TestAStageWithoutItsToolIsSkippedSilently` asserted that a missing tool was
*not* an error, on the grounds that "the dashboard already says the tool is
absent". That reasoning does not survive contact with the result panel, where
"no secrets found" and "nothing looked for secrets" are the same screen. It is
now `TestAStageWithoutItsToolIsReportedRatherThanSkippedSilently`, and the
partial case is reported for the same reason as the total one.

Pinned by `TestAScanThatCouldRunNoScannerIsNotACleanScan` and, in the view,
`TestAScanWithNoScannerInstalledIsReportedAsAFailure` — the inverted test from
phase 6, turned around, now also asserting that **nothing reaches the cache**.

**D22 — one stray `:` broke every scan, from every view, permanently.** Reported
from a real run, as a Trivy failure nobody could trace back to DevDesk:

Nothing upstream caught it: `internal/ui/oci_resources` performs no dependency check at all, unlike the security view (`view.go:147`). `ctrl+s`, `A`, `ctrl+a` and the delegated `LaunchBatchScanMsg` all reach the same `batchScanCmd`.

**Fix:** `Scan` records a missing tool as an error before any stage starts (`missingToolErrors`). One change in the package where the knowledge lives, and it closes the defect for every caller — **the OCI images view needed no change at all**, because its existing "errors and no findings" condition then reports the failure by itself. A pre-flight guard in the view was considered and dropped: with no scanner the scan returns instantly, so it buys nothing a clear error does not.

The precision that makes it usable is in **what is not reported**. A stage skipped because it does not apply to the target type is not missing anything — gitleaks scans a working tree, so a secret scan of an image was never going to run — and reporting those would train the user to ignore the warnings panel. Each message says what to install:

```
trivy: not available — nothing was scanned. Install trivy or pull aquasec/trivy
```

### This reverses a decision the tests had recorded

`TestAStageWithoutItsToolIsSkippedSilently` asserted that a missing tool was *not* an error, on the grounds that "the dashboard already says the tool is absent". That reasoning does not survive contact with the result panel, where "no secrets found" and "nothing looked for secrets" are the same screen. It is now `TestAStageWithoutItsToolIsReportedRatherThanSkippedSilently`, and the **partial** case is reported for the same reason as the total one.

## D22 — one stray `:` broke every scan, from every view, permanently

```
trivy vuln
exit status 1: FATAL flag error: unable to convert flags to options:
invalid server address format: parse ":": missing protocol scheme
```

The Trivy server field held `":"`. Nothing validated it — the value went straight from `m.trivyServerInput.Value()` into `--server` and into `config.yaml`. Three things compounded:

| | |
|---|---|
| A `:` typed into that field is a **character**, not the command line | Correct and deliberate: the placeholder is `https://trivy-server:4954`, so the field *has* to accept two colons — which is exactly why `alt+:` exists (§3.7). Now pinned by `TestAColonTypedIntoTheTrivyServerFieldIsACharacter`, so nobody fixes the wrong end of this. |
| The field is persisted on **every option toggle** | One keystroke reached the config file. |
| **Every view reads it from there** (`oci_resources/images.go:87`, `workspaces/actions.go:158`) | A field only ever seen in the security view broke image scans and workspace scans too, until the value was found by reading the YAML. |

**Fix**, in the three places that each own part of it:

- `serverAddr` trims, treats all-space as *unset*, and refuses anything that is not an absolute URL — checking `Hostname()` rather than `Host`, because `http://:` parses with a host of `":"` and no hostname. **All three builders** (`trivyArgs`, `trivyMisconfigArgs`, `sbomArgs`) go through it, so no stage can be the one that was not checked.
- The message names the setting rather than the parser, which is what makes it actionable from a view with no such field:
  ```
  trivy server address ":" is not a URL (want http://host:port) — fix or clear scan.trivy_server
  ```
- The security form refuses to start while the address is unusable (`scan.ValidateTrivyServer`, sharing the builders' rule so the two cannot disagree), and trims both the server and the Gitleaks config path before persisting.

Deliberately **not** done: silently dropping an unusable address, or rewriting the config on load. The user asked for client-server mode; running locally instead without saying so is the same class of quiet substitution as D20.

## Also

The inline gitleaks image default is folded into a `gitleaksImage()` helper mirroring `trivyImage()` — it was duplicated across two files.

content.text:
Deux PR ouvertes, CI verte sur les deux (race detector inclus).

## PR #27 — D20 + D22

**D20 — une image scannée sans scanner était rapportée comme saine.**
`Scan()` *saute* une étape dont l'outil manque au lieu de la faire échouer → aucune erreur, aucun finding → `scanOneImageCmd` conclut « propre », écrit zéro dans le cache avec un timestamp frais, et la Rule 126 l'y garde.

Corrigé dans `internal/scan` : `Scan` enregistre l'outil manquant comme erreur avant de démarrer les étapes. **La vue OCI n'a eu besoin d'aucun changement** — sa condition existante « erreurs ET aucun finding » remonte la panne toute seule. Le garde pré-vol dans la vue a été envisagé puis écarté : sans scanner le scan revient instantanément, il n'apporte rien de plus qu'un message clair.

Ce qui n'est **pas** signalé fait la qualité du correctif : une étape sautée parce qu'elle ne s'applique pas au type de cible (gitleaks lit un arbre de travail, donc jamais une image) n'est pas un outil manquant — les signaler entraînerait l'utilisateur à ignorer le panneau d'avertissements.

```
trivy: not available — nothing was scanned. Install trivy or pull aquasec/trivy
```

Ça a **inversé une décision inscrite dans les tests** : `TestAStageWithoutItsToolIsSkippedSilently` affirmait qu'un outil manquant n'était pas une erreur, « le dashboard le dit déjà ». Ce raisonnement ne survit pas au panneau de résultats, où « 0 secret trouvé » et « rien n'a cherché de secret » sont le même écran.

**D22 — ton erreur Trivy.** Le champ Server contenait `":"`. Trois choses se cumulaient :

| | |
|---|---|
| Un `:` tapé dans ce champ est un **caractère** | Correct et voulu — le placeholder est `https://trivy-server:4954`, le champ *doit* accepter deux `:`, c'est précisément pourquoi `alt+:` existe (§3.7). Maintenant épinglé par un test, pour que personne ne « corrige » le mauvais bout. |
| Le champ est persisté à **chaque toggle d'option** | Une frappe atteignait `config.yaml`. |
| **Toutes les vues le lisent depuis là** | Un champ visible seulement dans la vue security cassait aussi les scans d'images et de workspaces. |

`serverAddr` trim, traite tout-espaces comme *non défini*, et refuse ce qui n'est pas une URL absolue — en testant `Hostname()` et pas `Host`, car `http://:` parse avec un host de `":"` et aucun hostname. Les **trois** builders passent par là. Le message nomme le réglage, pas le parser :

```
trivy server address ":" is not a URL (want http://host:port) — fix or clear scan.trivy_server
```

Écarté volontairement : ignorer silencieusement une adresse inutilisable, ou réécrire la config au chargement — ce serait la même substitution silencieuse que D20.

> **Pour ta machine :** vide le champ Server dans la vue security, ou supprime `trivy_server` de `~/.devdesk/contexts/<ctx>/config.yaml`. Sans ça les scans échoueront encore, mais désormais avec le message ci-dessus au lieu du FATAL Trivy.

## PR #28 — le retour à la ligne manquant

Trouvé la cause et, surtout, pourquoi le test évident n'aurait rien attrapé : les deux colonnes sont des listes de lignes **indépendantes**, zippées à la fin. La ligne sous « Scan Options » *à l'écran* appartient à la colonne de droite (« Gitleaks Options »). L'espacement vertical est une propriété d'une colonne — l'affirmer sur le rendu passerait pour une mauvaise raison.

Les deux constructeurs sont donc extraits (`formLeftColumn` / `formRightColumn`) et le test vérifie chaque colonne séparément. Vérifié en retirant le correctif : le test échoue bien en nommant la ligne percutée.

Coverage 80.7 % → 80.9 %, nouveau code à 100 %. Je merge les deux ?

true only on the topology tab, where `InEditMode()` is unconditionally false. It
could never fire. Deleted, along with its one implementation;
`TestCommandModeOnTheTopologyTab` became
`TestTheTopologyTabNeverBlocksCommandMode` and records why.

### 3.8 Docker registry groups

Two shapes have to be supported: a remote registry with or without
authentication, and a **group** fronting several remote registries, itself
reachable anonymously or not. The second is the one the current model cannot
express.

Not started. The decisions below are settled; one is not, and is marked as such.

#### What the current code does

| Concern | Today | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Parent/child relation | in memory only, for the lifetime of one browser session | `registry_browser.go:26` (`browserRegistryEntry`) |
| Group discovery | Nexus REST, re-run on **every** browser open, 8 s timeout each, behind a blocking spinner | `registry_browser.go:153`, `registrymgr/nexus.go` |
| Member URLs | synthesised as `host + /repository/<memberName>`, alias stripped of `-proxy`/`-hosted`/`-local` | `nexus.go:111`, `nexus.go:200` |
| Credential inheritance | member searches use the **parent's** URL as the `~/.docker/config.json` lookup key | `browser_keys.go:130` |
| Registries tab | flat table, no indication a group was ever found | `table.go:182` |
| Result filter (`r`) | cycles member URLs; no group level | `browser_tags.go:25` |

`RegistryConfig.Registries` is a flat `[]RegistryItem` and carries no parent
field. Nothing about a group survives closing the browser: it is rediscovered,
over the network, next time.

The credential inheritance is the one piece that already behaves correctly, and
the reason it does is the same reason the open decision below is hard.

#### Settled

| Ref | Decision |
|---|---|
| A | **One list, one discriminator, one parent pointer** — `kind: registry \| group` plus `parent` on `RegistryItem`. Two parallel lists and a recursive `Children` tree were both rejected. |
| 1 | The parent is referenced by **slug**, not by URL. |
| 3 | Discovered members live in a **disk cache**, not in `config.yaml`. |
| 4 | The Registries tab gets **drill-down** navigation (`←` / `→`), not an indented tree and not a `Group` column. |
| 5 | **No purely logical groups.** A group always corresponds to a real repository-manager group. |
| F | `provider` is a **declared field**, not sniffed from the URL. |

**A — one list.** A Nexus group *is* a pullable registry as well as a container,
so splitting `registries` and `registry_groups` would have duplicated the form,
the table and the credential handling to model a distinction the server does not
make. A single list with a discriminator keeps one table, one form (fields shown
per `kind`), and leaves sorting and filtering intact.

**1 — slug over URL.** The URL is today's de facto identifier and is threaded
through `registryLoginStatus`, the scan cache keys and the message types, which
is exactly why it is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on: editing a group's
URL would silently orphan its members. The slug replaces the URL **only as the
parent link and the cache key** — everything Docker-facing stays keyed on the
URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on. Existing configs migrate by
deriving a slug from the alias, falling back to the URL host; uniqueness has to
be enforced at load, and the form needs to reject a collision rather than accept
a config that will not round-trip.

**3 — cache, not config.** Discovered members are derived data with a server as
their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares. Putting them
in the cache mirrors `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` (Rule 126) rather
than inventing a fourth persistence shape:
`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`, keyed by group slug, refreshed
explicitly with `ctrl+r` on a group row. The browser then reads config plus
cache and opens instantly and offline, which is what removes D13's blocking
state rather than papering over it. A `Members` column showing the count and
`theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` (Rule 127) is what keeps staleness visible —
without it, a silently stale cache is worse than the current re-detection.

**4 — drill-down.** Level 1 lists groups and standalone registries; `→` enters a
group and lists its members; `←` goes back, with a breadcrumb below the table
(Rules 111, 123). The indented-tree alternative reads faster at five registries
but breaks the moment the table is sorted or the FilterBar (Rule 136) narrows
it, and drill-down is already the pattern `gitlab-explorer` uses. Proposed
columns: `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.

**5 — no logical groups.** Grouping unrelated registries under a user-invented
name was considered and dropped: it has no server to discover from, no shared
credential to inherit, and no group URL to pull through, so it would be a
display-only concept carrying the weight of a real one. If the need for
arbitrary grouping appears later it is a saved-selection feature in the browser,
not a change to the registry model.

**F — declared provider.** `NexusDetector.CanHandle` currently returns true
whenever `ManagementURL` is non-empty (`nexus.go:31`), which makes that field do
double duty as an implicit "this is Nexus" flag and makes the detector list
effectively single-vendor. A `provider` field on the group — `nexus`, `harbor`,
`artifactory`, `gitlab`, `generic` — turns `CanHandle` into a match on a
declared value, with the generic detector last. It is a cycle field in the form
(Rule 132) and it is what makes a second implementation possible without
guessing.

#### Open: how far credential inheritance goes

The concrete case: a Nexus group **with** authentication fronting eight Nexus
proxies. Browsing the proxy that points at `dhi.io` has to query the *proxy's*
URL while authenticating with the *group's* credentials.

That much the code already does — `submitSearch` sets
`credURL = parentURL ?: entry.URL` — and the reason it works is worth stating
explicitly, because it constrains everything else:

> **`docker login` takes a registry host, not a path.** `~/.docker/config.json`
> is keyed on `host[:port]`, so the group and all eight proxies share one single
> credential entry, because they share `nexus.example.com`.

Three consequences:

- `inherit` is not a convenience for path-based groups, it is the **only** thing
  the credential store can represent. Every member of such a group authenticates
  identically whether the model says so or not.
- A per-member `credentials` override is **not storable today**. It would need a
  secret keyed by slug rather than by registry URL, which `docker login` cannot
  represent.

  §3.9 changes what this costs, without changing the conclusion. DevDesk now has
  a store — the host's, keyed by whatever string it likes — so a slug-keyed
  password is no longer unstorable in principle, and it would not put plaintext
  anywhere. What it would still do is take DevDesk out of `docker login`'s model
  and into maintaining its own registry auth, for a case (§3.8) that has not been
  shown to exist. `RegistryItem` still has no password field by construction, and
  that is still the right default.
- What a member *can* usefully override is **`anonymous`**: do not send the
  group's credentials to this one. That is representable, costs nothing, and is
  the safety valve — and it is the same mechanism D12 needs.

Proposed, pending the discussion: replace `AuthEnabled bool` with an `AuthMode`
cycle field where a group is `anonymous | credentials` and a member is
`inherit | anonymous`. The four cases in scope then map cleanly:

| Case | Group | Member |
|---|---|---|
| Remote registry, no auth | — | `kind: registry`, `anonymous` |
| Remote registry, auth | — | `kind: registry`, `credentials` |
| Group with auth, 8 proxies (the case above) | `credentials` | `inherit` |
| Anonymous group | `anonymous` | `inherit` |

What still needs deciding is whether a member-level `credentials` is worth
supporting at all. It only becomes meaningful for a group whose members are on
different hosts, which decision 5 has just ruled out of the model — so the
current reading is that it should not exist, and that a genuine need for it is a
separate decision about who stores the password.

**Adjacent question to settle before the model is frozen: browse and pull may
not share a URL.** Path-based Nexus access answers the registry API at
`/repository/<name>/v2/...`, which is what `registryAPIURL` builds and what the
tag search relies on. Whether `docker pull` accepts the same path-form reference
depends on the deployment — a dedicated HTTP connector port per repository is
the older Nexus arrangement, path routing needs a reverse proxy in front. If
they differ, a member needs a third URL alongside `url` and `management_url`,
and `multiImageName` (`browser_tags.go:125`) is building an unpullable
reference today. **This should be checked against the actual Nexus instance**
rather than reasoned about; it is one `docker pull` away from being answered.

#### Sequencing — **prerequisite met**

This lands in `internal/ui/oci_resources`, and the rule was: surface tests, then
split, then complete coverage, and only then the feature. All three are done.
Phase 4 split the package (no file is over the 800-line ceiling; the former
822-line `registry_browser.go` is 243) and phase 6 finished the coverage, so
**§3.8 is unblocked and can start on the feature directly.**

What is under it now, in the files this feature rewrites:

| File | Coverage | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| `browser_keys.go` | 78.1 % | the search form and the tags keymap |
| `browser_tags.go` | ~97 % | sort, both filters, tag actions |
| `browser_view.go` | ~99 % | the grouped form, the results table, the filter bar |
| `commands.go` | 88.0 % | group detection against `httptest`, incl. the management-URL credential lookup |

Service implementation on Linux, through one storage and one only.

#### What was wrong

Three of the five storage paths were plaintext on disk, and the option the UI
labelled "secure" was one of them.

| Secret | Destination | Protection |
|---|---|---|
| Forge token | `~/.devdesk/credentials-<ctx>.json` | **plaintext JSON**, 0600 |
| Forge token | `gitlab.token` in `contexts/<ctx>/config.yaml` | **plaintext YAML** |
| Forge token | git credential helper | whatever the helper does |
| Registry password | `~/.docker/config.json` via `docker login` | whatever Docker's `credsStore` does |
| Registry password | `registry.password` in `config.yaml` | **plaintext YAML**, read at `explorer/create.go:43,132` |

`ChainStorage.Save` wrote to **every** storage in the chain, and all three
construction sites built it as `NewChainStorage(FileStorage,
GitCredentialStorage)`. Choosing **"Save to Git Credential Manager (secure)"**
therefore stored the token in the credential manager *and* in
`~/.devdesk/credentials-<context>.json` in plaintext. Reads made it worse:
`FileStorage` was first and `ChainStorage.Load` returned the first hit, so the
plaintext file was authoritative and the credential manager was never consulted
while it existed. The secure backend was decorative in both directions.

The other option was no better in a different way: **"Save token to config file
(less secure)"** set `saveToHelper = false`, so nothing reached the chain and
the token landed only in `config.yaml`. Both options put the token in plaintext;
the "secure" one did it twice.

And logout did not clean up: `handleLogoutComplete` cleared
`m.config.GitLab.Token` in memory with no `config.Save` behind it, so the token
survived in `contexts/<ctx>/config.yaml`.

#### The distinction that decided the design

Delegating to `git credential` delegates to **whatever helper git happens to be
configured with**. If that is `store`, the token lands in `~/.git-credentials`
in plaintext — the same failure, relocated. Only `manager` (GCM),
`osxkeychain`, `libsecret` and `wincred` reach a real OS store. "Goes through
git credential" is not the same claim as "encrypted at rest", and the
=== DEFECTS ===

the test **inverted** — asserting the current behaviour and saying so. D9, D10
and D11 each had one, and each failed the moment the fix landed, which is how
the stale test and the stale backlog entry got found together.

### 1.3 Open

D12–D14 sit in `internal/ui/oci_resources` and are cheap on their own, but
§3.8 rewrites the code path each of them lives in. Fix them **as part of** that
work rather than ahead of it, and write each one's test inverted first, per the
pattern above. D14's inverted test now exists.

**D21** also sits in that package but is **independent of §3.8** and should not
wait for it. It is three lines of dead code with its invariant already pinned,
so it belongs in whatever next touches `connectivity_form.go`.

D20 and D22 are fixed — see §1.1.

D15–D19 were found by the phase 5 pass, were unrelated to §3.8, and are fixed —
see §1.1. Each had been recorded with an inverted test asserting the broken
behaviour; those tests are what failed when the fix landed, and each has been
turned around to assert the fixed behaviour instead.

**D12 — `AuthEnabled` has no effect on browse or discovery.** The flag is
honoured in exactly three places: the `docker login` fired on form submit, the
`Logged` column, and the URL list `registryLoginStatusCmd` checks. Neither code
path that actually talks to a registry consults it. `submitSearch`
(`browser_keys.go:142`) calls `docker.GetStoredCreds(credURL)`
unconditionally and hands the result to `searchRegistryTagsCmd`;
`detectRegistryGroupCmd` (`commands.go:563`) does the same before calling into
`registrymgr`. A registry the user has marked as needing no authentication will
still have the host's stored credentials sent to it whenever any other registry
on that host has been logged into — which, given that Docker keys credentials by
host, is the normal case for a Nexus instance. This is the defect the
`anonymous` mode in §3.8 exists to make expressible; today there is no way to
say "do not send credentials here" at all.

**D13 — the browser cannot be dismissed while it is resolving.**
`handleKeyMsg` returns `nil` for every key in `browserStateResolving`
(`browser_keys.go:70`), `esc` included, and that state is entered
unconditionally on open whenever any registry is configured. The detections run
concurrently with an 8 s timeout each, so the wedge is bounded at roughly eight
seconds — but it is eight seconds during which the application ignores the user,
on a screen they may have opened by mistake. §3.8 removes the state rather than
the symptom: with members read from config and cache, there is nothing to
resolve and the form renders immediately.

A smaller thing in the same handler, not worth its own entry:
`HandleGroupDetected` matches the incoming result against `reg.URL`, so two
registries configured with the same URL collide and the second result overwrites
the first. The slug introduced in §3.8 is the natural key to match on instead.

**D14 — the registry filter shows a raw URL for group members.**
`registryFilterLabel()` (`browser_tags.go:63`) resolves the active filter by
searching `b.registries`, which holds only the configured top-level entries.
Discovered members are not in that list, so filtering to one falls through to
returning `b.registryFilter` — the full synthesised URL — where every other row
in the same view shows a short alias. The fix follows from §3.8 rather than
preceding it: once members are persisted they are resolvable, and the filter
gains a group level at the same time.

Pinned inverted by `TestAGroupMembersFilterLabelIsStillARawURL`, which asserts
the raw URL today and asserts the configured registry's alias alongside it as
the contrast.

**D21 — an unreachable focus clamp in `ConnectivityTestForm`.** Dead code, not a
user-visible defect, and the same shape as D5 in `CreationForm`.

The `left` and `right` handlers (`connectivity_form.go:242`, `:253`) clamp the
focus after cycling the test type, guarding against the field count shrinking

## Formatting

- **gofmt** and **goimports** are mandatory — no style debates

- Accept interfaces, return structs
- Keep interfaces small (1-3 methods)

## Error Handling

Always wrap errors with context:

```go
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("failed to create user: %w", err)
}
```

## Reference

See skill: `golang-patterns` for comprehensive Go idioms and patterns.

```go
apiKey := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
```

  ```bash
  gosec ./...
  ```

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
```

1	package ociresources
2	
3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
11	)
12	
13	const registryFormMaxField = 6 // 0=URL, 1=Username, 2=Password, 3=Alias, 4=AuthEnabled, 5=NexusURL, 6=Submit
14	
15	// RegistryFormSubmitMsg is sent when the registry form is submitted
16	type RegistryFormSubmitMsg struct {
17		Index    int // -1 for new, >= 0 for edit
18		Item     config.RegistryItem
19		Password string // not stored in config; used for docker login
20	}
21	
22	// RegistryFormCancelMsg is sent when the registry form is cancelled
23	type RegistryFormCancelMsg struct{}
24	
25	// RegistryForm is a form for adding or editing a registry entry
26	type RegistryForm struct {
27		index         int // -1 = new, >=0 = edit
28		width         int
29		urlInput      textinput.Model
30		usernameInput textinput.Model
31		passwordInput textinput.Model
32		aliasInput    textinput.Model
33		nexusURLInput textinput.Model
34		authEnabled   bool
35		focusedField  int
36		err           string
37	}
38	
39	// NewRegistryForm creates a form for adding a new registry
40	func NewRegistryForm(width int) *RegistryForm {
41		return newRegistryForm(-1, config.RegistryItem{AuthEnabled: true}, width)
42	}
43	
44	// NewRegistryEditForm creates a form for editing an existing registry
45	func NewRegistryEditForm(index int, item config.RegistryItem, width int) *RegistryForm {
46		return newRegistryForm(index, item, width)
47	}
48	
49	func newRegistryForm(index int, item config.RegistryItem, width int) *RegistryForm {
50		urlInput := textinput.New()
51		urlInput.CharLimit = 256
52		urlInput.Placeholder = "registry.example.com"
53		theme.StyleTextInput(&urlInput)
54		urlInput.SetValue(item.URL)
55		urlInput.Focus()
56	
57		usernameInput := textinput.New()
58		usernameInput.CharLimit = 128
59		usernameInput.Placeholder = "username"
60		theme.StyleTextInput(&usernameInput)
61		usernameInput.SetValue(item.Username)
62	
63		passwordInput := textinput.New()
64		passwordInput.CharLimit = 256
65		passwordInput.Placeholder = "password"
66		passwordInput.EchoMode = textinput.EchoPassword
67		passwordInput.EchoCharacter = '•'
68		theme.StyleTextInput(&passwordInput)
69	
70		aliasInput := textinput.New()
71		aliasInput.CharLimit = 32
72		aliasInput.Placeholder = "gl"
73		theme.StyleTextInput(&aliasInput)
74		aliasInput.SetValue(item.Alias)
75	
76		nexusURLInput := textinput.New()
77		nexusURLInput.CharLimit = 512
78		nexusURLInput.Placeholder = "https://registry-mgr.example.com/path/to/group  (optional)"
79		theme.StyleTextInput(&nexusURLInput)
80		nexusURLInput.SetValue(item.ManagementURL)
81	
82		f := &RegistryForm{
83			index:         index,
84			width:         width,
85			urlInput:      urlInput,
86			usernameInput: usernameInput,
87			passwordInput: passwordInput,
88			aliasInput:    aliasInput,
89			nexusURLInput: nexusURLInput,
90			authEnabled:   item.AuthEnabled,
91		}
92		f.resizeInputs()
93		return f
94	}
95	
96	// SetWidth updates the form width and resizes inputs accordingly.
97	func (f *RegistryForm) SetWidth(w int) {
98		f.width = w
99		f.resizeInputs()
100	}
101	
102	func (f *RegistryForm) resizeInputs() {
103		// Label overhead: viewport border (2) + indent (2) + longest label "Nexus URL " + chevron + spaces (~16)
104		const labelOverhead = 18
105		w := max(f.width-labelOverhead, 20)
106		f.urlInput.Width = w

121	// Update handles messages for the registry form
122	func (f *RegistryForm) Update(msg tea.Msg) (*RegistryForm, tea.Cmd) {
123		switch msg := msg.(type) {
124		case tea.KeyMsg:
125			return f.handleKeyMsg(msg)
126		}
127		return f.updateActiveInput(msg)
